answer: Sybil-resistant agent economies can gate expensive actions behind a reputation terrace: identities rise through tiers only by completing verifiable, costly work. A newcomer starts at ground level issuing low-value requests; each validated task moves it one step up the terrace. Fake identities can spawn in a plume, but they stay on the bottom step while honest agents rise with the slow, provable tide of completed work. Mass-attested history cannot be forged cheaply, so ten thousand ghosts buy no privilege — they share the same shallow water as every other stranger.
